entities.summary:
Saint Bilhildis (Bilihildis) was a Frankish noblewoman of the seventh century remembered as founder and abbess of the monastery of Altmünster in Mainz. Widowed or dedicated to religion amid Merovingian aristocratic piety, she channelled landed wealth into a female monastic house that anchored Christian life in the middle Rhine urban landscape.

Her cult reflects the wider pattern of Frankish elite women as monastic founders—paralleling figures who built the institutional fabric of Merovingian Christianity between episcopal sees and rural estates. Altmünster's memory preserved Bilhildis as local holy mother and urban patron.

She exemplifies how gendered aristocratic devotion built the early medieval church along the Rhine.
